literal: Carrying away knowing, water those who leap indeed like; failing knowing, what having sulked?
translation: Like those who leap into a stream knowing it will sweep them away, what is the use of my sulking when I know my resolve will fail?
modern: நீர் தங்களை அடித்துச் செல்லும் என்று அறிந்தும் அதில் குதிப்பவர்களைப் போல, என் ஊடல் தோற்றுப்போகும் என்று தெரிந்தும் நான் ஊடல் கொள்வதால் என்ன பயன்?
explanation: The speaker reflects on the futility of her feigned anger towards her lover. She compares herself to someone who jumps into a fast-flowing stream, fully aware that the current will inevitably sweep them away. Similarly, she knows that her resolve to stay angry will instantly fail ('பொய்த்தல்') the moment she sees him. The couplet beautifully captures the overpowering nature of love, showing that intellectual awareness of one's weakness cannot stop the emotional surrender.
